description: Issued purchase-order PDF -> sent message -> supplier reply -> served app_purchase_order status, and an explicit gap for every PO without a linked send (operating/issued_sends.py): one bounded GET-only mail capture of the purchasing Sent Items and the hub mailbox's inbox (examples/issued_sends_mail_capture_scope.live-check.json) and one GET-only SharePoint capture of the Portal's procurement folder with DocumentCategory (examples/issued_sends_sharepoint_capture_scope.live-check.json) into {tmp}/state, read back as staff:purchasing, plus the Portal PO relation through the source mirror. Counts only: sends by kind, renders by origin, byte matches by basis, chain outcomes and replies, PO gaps by kind and reason.
notes: Live-unverified until the live check runs it (module tests are injected-transport). A send is a message in a mailbox's own Sent Items whose From is that mailbox; a subject starting '[STAGING → ' (plx-customer-portal email-redirect.ts, every non-production provider send) is a test_redirect: counted, never matched, never evidence. A vendor send's attachment named like a Portal PO PDF links to a captured render only by equal bytes (sha256, else quickXorHash); a name alone is a lead. A reply is a message in the send's conversation from a domain it went to, received after it. The legacy send path (purchase-order-legacy-send.ts, Resend from noreply@) keeps no mailbox copy, and the PDF route keeps the same ISSUED_PO render with no send, so every PO without a linked send is a gap (send_not_captured or send_not_linked) with its reasons, never 'not sent'. Expected honest gaps: the reporting API serves the staging replica while real sends come from production (chain_outcomes.po_not_served until go-live), every staging send is redirected, and most served POs have no captured send (gap_reasons.no_render_captured); the procurement folder comes from Portal code defaults and may not exist (sources.sharepoint.complete false, capture_runs.sharepoint.reasons). When the Portal fails the PO relation the output names it in blocked_upstream and expect_blocked holds. Counts are recorded, never asserted. BC is optional_env: the command's live readers (operating.case_runtime.build_live_readers) build a BC reader when its variables are set, which this check never reads; undeclared, the runner stopped the command at that read (undeclared_env BC_CLIENT_SECRET), and required, a host without BC would skip a check that does not need it. When Graph refused every in-scope mailbox with HTTP 403 or 401 (integrations/capture_mail.refused_parts, the one Graph part shape of capture_mail.graph_block) blocked_upstream also names the refused mail call (mail.mailbox_lookup or mail.folder_read) with error_code missing_permission and its missing application permission on 403 (User.Read.All; Mail.Read, which an Exchange application access policy may also scope out), or error_code unauthorized on 401, cause host_misconfiguration, and expect_blocked holds when the rest read something (source_read.inputs_read >= 1 over mail, SharePoint renders and PO rows) and mail, the one input a pass requires, read messages unless a part stopped it (source_read.unblocked_unread empty).
